brief: Goldman's TMT morning wrap for Oct 6, 2026. Mostly reports a risk-on backdrop rather than arguing one: Nasdaq futures +60bps to new highs, global bond yields easing (US 10yr -3bps to 5.27%), WTI -2% to $87, Le Pen's deficit-reduction proposal lifting French sentiment, Bessent saying the US can bend the debt curve quickly, and Yemen/Saudi Middle East supply developments. In TMT: Alphabet signed a 20-year, 890MW nuclear deal with Constellation Energy ($4.3bn build-out); Seagate and Toshiba are bidding for TDK's hard-drive-head unit; AMD's Su says chip demand stays very high for years and is outpacing supply, reaffirming a $10bn Taiwan investment; NVDA nears $6T market cap after its buyback; Pinterest hired an Amazon veteran as CFO. Three embedded research pieces do argue: GS raises SPCX's AI-segment forecasts and $230 target, calling its estimates still conservative versus Street; GS frames NFLX's selloff as reversible on new hit content, modeling content spend growing slower than revenue while advertising gains momentum; GS reiterates TSMC Buy (TP NT$3,300), raising 2027-28E capex to $85bn/$98bn on broadening AI demand, and separately downgrades GNTX while preferring Industrial Tech over Autos into 3Q26.
